summary: This note describes Radulphe, a French monk who left his monastery without his superiors' permission and travelled to the Rhine Valley during the Second Crusade (1147–49). There he preached that Jews should be slain as enemies of the Christian religion. The note is very short and gives no further biographical detail.
one_line: Radulphe, a French monk who preached violence against Jews in the Rhine Valley during the Second Crusade (1147–49).
key_facts: Radulphe is also spelled Radulph or Rodolphe.
Radulphe left his monastery in France without permission from his superiors.
Radulphe travelled to the Rhine Valley during the Second Crusade.
The Second Crusade took place from 1147 to 1149.
Radulphe preached that the Jews should be slain as the enemies of the Christian religion.
The quoted preaching is: "that the Jews should be slain as the enemies of the Christian religion."
